question: What math problem types, datasets, LLM techniques, influencing factors and open challenges define LLM-based mathematical reasoning?
contributions: Overview of math problem types and datasets (arithmetic, MWP, geometry, ATP, vision-language)
Three-level taxonomy of methods: prompting frozen LLMs, strategies enhancing frozen LLMs, fine-tuning
Analysis of robustness, factors affecting arithmetic skill, and a mathematics pedagogy perspective

results.claim: Yuan et al. found that larger models generally do better at arithmetic but plateau, with Galactica similar at 30B and 120B.
results.setup: Arithmetic evaluation of GPT series and open LLMs; survey gives no accuracy numbers
results.quote: Larger models generally perform better, but a performance plateau is observed, as shown by Galactica’s similar outcomes at 30B and 120B parameters.
results.note: Quote contains 30B and 120B as stated; value left null because it is not a measured accuracy.

results.claim: Chain-of-thought is described as the first method to steer LLMs to step-by-step math reasoning; Self-Consistency samples several CoT paths and uses consistency to find a more probable answer.
results.source: Wei et al., 2022; Wang et al., 2023
results.setup: Qualitative description in Sec 4.2; no numbers

results.claim: Program-of-Thought separates computation from reasoning: the LM writes a program and an external computer executes it.
The survey names LLM brittleness: inconsistent across textual forms, different answers across reasoning paths on repeated trials, and vulnerable to adversarial inputs.

limits: Pure survey: reports no experiments, accuracy figures or effect sizes for CoT, PAL, PoT or Self-Consistency; do not cite for any effect size.
Method descriptions are one or two sentences each with no hyperparameters, prompts or settings.
No appendix, no limitations section; no explicit coverage method for the literature search.
Coverage is of 2023-era models (GPT-3, ChatGPT, GPT-4, PaLM 2); has dated.
practices: Do not rely on accuracy alone when evaluating LLM math; also assess confidence and verifiable explanations (Sec 4.2).
Using adversarial samples in few-shot prompts improves robustness (Zhou et al. 2023b, Sec 5.1).
Combine CoT with an external tool such as a Python REPL to correct reasoning errors (Yamauchi et al. 2023, Sec 4.2).
Design math LLM output for the user (student) comprehension, not just correctness (Sec 6).
